title: Onboard embeddings + reranker: canary variant harness and bundled performance profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create a repeatable onboarding flow that packages an embedding+reranker model pair into a single performance profile bundle, validates it through a canary variant harness, pins the approved version in the catalog, and publishes the profile artifacts for runtime consumption. Scope includes: (1) automated micro-benchmarks for embeddings (throughput, cosine stability) and reranker (NDCG@10, recall@K, latency distribution), (2) a canary runner that exercises the candidate variant under representative traffic slices, (3) manifest/metadata schema for bundled profiles (model pair + quantization profile + batching hints + KV cache expectations), (4) integration with the pinning pipeline so the bundle becomes a pin-able catalog artifact, and (5) publish step to the profile registry + automated dashboarding for review. This ticket focuses on the engineering glue and gating logic; downstream work will be follow-ups for UX in Console and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical bundle schema (JSON manifest) exists and is validated by unit tests
Automated micro-benchmarks run in CI and emit metrics for embeddings and reranker (p50/p95 latency, throughput, memory)
Canary harness can be triggered from the catalog to run a 1-hour smoke validation on a subset of traffic with configurable traffic weight
Gating rules implemented: block publish if reranker NDCG@10 drops >2% relative to baseline OR p95 latency increases >25% OR embeddings cosine drift >0.03
Successful publish writes bundle artifacts (model ids, quantization tag, profiling metrics, manifest) to the profile registry and produces a signed pin entry consumable by Dedicated/Private runtimes
End-to-end test that creates a bundle, runs canary, and exercises a rollback path exists in the integration test suite

blockers: Intermittent p95 spikes during staging canary runs — needs profiling (GPU kernel scheduling)
Catalog API rate limits when registering large bundles (throttling observed)
risks: False positives: overly strict gating could block good variants and slow onboarding velocity
Bundle size and artifact proliferation could increase registry storage and retrieval latency
Quantized variants may show acceptable accuracy in micro-bench but regress on long-context integration tests
